parsed.study_design: Ecological descriptive secondary analysis of Population Census, National Sample Survey, and municipal-finance data across states and urban-settlement size classes
parsed.population_and_sample: Urban households aggregated by Indian state and urban-settlement size class; municipal-finance evidence from urban local bodies in seven major states
parsed.exposure: Urban-governance and municipal-finance arrangements, including the 74th Constitutional Amendment, fiscal decentralization, reduced intergovernmental transfers, local revenue capacity, and increasing reliance on financial institutions
parsed.outcome: Household coverage by drinking-water supply and toilet/sanitation facilities, including lack of latrines and disparities by state and settlement size
parsed.rationale: Section 3 (pp. 16–23) empirically analyzes Census and NSS household coverage by drinking water and toilets across states, years, and settlement-size classes. Section 4 (pp. 23–28) examines governance and administrative exposures—including decentralization, municipal fiscal capacity, declining transfers, and the 74th Constitutional Amendment—and relates them to unequal provision of water and sanitation services, supported by municipal-revenue data from the cited NIPFP study.
